notes: Template-references-missing-input-asset is a workflow-level completeness bug every fresh user hits. No gsl template in the 64-template catalog, but reproducible as a synthetic ready template with a LoadImage pointing at a nonexistent file; port check/validation flagging unbundled inputs is the checkable contract. Known asset URL gives a clean right answer.

Shipped-with-bypassed-node is a classic template defect affecting everyone who runs it as-is. VibeComfy inspect can statically detect a bypassed node mode in a template graph; fix (un-bypass) is verifiable. No hidream template in catalog, so needs a synthetic or imported template to exercise.

Root cause is an outdated ComfyUI install, not the workflow; the traceback is environment-version noise. Nothing workflow-level for VibeComfy validation to catch, and reproducing requires pinning an old ComfyUI build.

Audio static/popping tied to a specific GPU (RTX 4080 Super) and ComfyUI version regression; fix is 'downgrade ComfyUI'. No workflow or template change to test, no MiniMax H3 template in catalog, and audio-quality regression needs human listening on that hardware.

VAEDecodeTiled is categorically incompatible with MiniMax H3 VAE (built-in tiling) — a deterministic node-choice error affecting all H3 users. Exercisable by editing a template to swap in the tiled decode and asserting the NestedTensor/argument error class at load/run; needs H3 weights (no H3 template in catalog), hence medium repro. Maintainer-confirmed right answer.

Mostly a torch-version environment bug (fix: upgrade torch 2.11) plus WSL/triton build issues; overlaps #15274's actual node-incompatibility finding. VibeComfy can't meaningfully exercise a torch wheel mismatch, and the mixed issue muddies the verifiable contract.

Attention-implementation choice (sage vs sdpa) silently degrading Wan 2.2 temporal coherence is a real workflow-level trade-off. Testable against wan22_i2v_comfy_lightx2v by toggling attention and comparing frame-to-frame variance programmatically, but it requires actual GPU generation and flicker is a statistical judgment, so verification is softer than a validation error.

KJNodes-specific crop behavior: floor-rounding is by-design and the 64x64 placeholder-mask IndexError stems from ComfyUI's LoadImage UI flow, not the workflow graph. Nothing in VibeComfy templates/validation touches the mask-editor path; one node pack's edge case, not a workflow-level problem.

Checkpoint/code version mismatch (LTX-2 vs LTX-2.3 weights) producing scale_shift_table size-mismatch at model load is a top-tier failure class for a catalog heavy on LTX 2.3 audio templates. Deterministic load-time error, maintainer-stated right answer (match weight version to node pack); repro needs the wrong weights downloaded, hence medium.

Textbook testable constraint: non-16-divisible resolution (800x456) deterministically crashes audio cross-attention reshape in InfiniteTalk/MultiTalk. Maps directly to wanvideo_wrapper_21_14b_v2v_infinitetalk — resolution is a template parameter VC can set; the divisibility rule is statically checkable at validate time and the fix (832x480) is OP-confirmed.

Real, well-evidenced issue; many wanvideo_wrapper templates contain BlockSwap so the fix (swap to 'WanVideo Enhanced BlockSwap') is a schema-checkable edit. But the actual failure is host-level pinned-memory RAM growth on Windows across repeated runs — not reproducible via VibeComfy validation or a single template run.

Classic real-world failure: degraded/muddy output from missing required distill LoRA (plus xformers). LTX-2.3 templates wire the distill LoRA, so a test can strip it and assert detection (doctor --models / wiring inspection); full symptom confirmation needs a render, keeping repro at medium.
MiniMax-H3 GGUF support lives in a third-party fork; VibeComfy has no MiniMax-H3 template and no loader to exercise. Issue is fork-specific model support, not a workflow-level problem.
AMD AOTriton kernel crash fixed by a core PR — hardware/driver-specific, no MiniMax template to port, and nothing at the workflow layer for VibeComfy validation to catch.

Node-internal sageattention version/arch check bug; requires live ComfyUI runtime with the H3 patch node. No VibeComfy template uses it and the failure is runtime Python, not schema/structure, so validation tooling cannot trigger it.

Host-level 0.31 performance regression (wall-clock doubling, disk thrash) on specific GPUs. Needs timed generation runs on the affected hardware; no MiniMax template and no workflow-layer defect, so unverifiable via VibeComfy.
ROCm mmap per-tensor load-time defect fixed by a server flag; load performance is outside workflow scope and VibeComfy templates expose no mmap path. Cannot be exercised or verified.

WAN 2.2 weight-loading OOM (pinned memory, multi-GPU) hits a broad user base and VibeComfy does ship wan22 templates, but the failure is intermittent host/core-level at load time — validation can't reproduce it and a run test needs the exact multi-GPU setup.
WSL-specific comfy-aimdo dlopen defect surfaced only through a custom LoRA trainer; far outside VibeComfy's template/validation surface.

Textbook custom-node/API drift ('unexpected keyword argument' after upstream change) — exactly the class VibeComfy's object_info schemas cache, port check, and nodes install-plan exist to catch; a drift-detection test can be built against any KJNodes-based template even though no template uses this specific H3 attention node. Fixed upstream, so the right answer is checkable.

Classic real-world dependency break (kornia 0.8.x dropped `pad` re-export) killing the whole LTXVideo pack so its nodes show as missing — the exact class of failure `vibecomfy port check`/doctor (missing class_type) flags. Not fully reproducible repo-only since it needs the broken kornia version installed at runtime, hence reproducibility medium; solution is known and confirmed.

Duplicate of the same import-failure class as #553/#538 but vaguer ('several nodes error after install') with only reinstall/git-pull workarounds; no specific broken module or node named, so nothing concrete to assert in a test.

Directly exercises an existing ready template: image/z_image wires an empty CLIPTextEncode as negative (same ConditioningZeroOut/empty-negative debate), so graph-inspection and CFG>1 distortion can be reproduced and reasoned about in VibeComfy. Right answer not fully settled (CFG=1 vs empty CLIP Text Encode), so solution_verifiability medium rather than high.

Template references a nonexistent node type (GeminiNanoBanana2V2) plus stale widgets_values order — precisely what `vibecomfy validate --json` unknown-node and value_not_in_list checks exist for, giving a binary pass/fail. Closest analog is VibeComfy's image-edit templates; the fix (republish against current schema) is concretely verifiable.

Exact template match: VibeComfy has audio/ace_step_1_5_t2a_song importing EmptyAceStep1_5LatentAudio/TextEncodeAceStepAudio1_5, so missing-core-node and get_object_info-crash-on-missing-model-dirs reproduce cleanly via inspect/doctor against an older ComfyUI checkout; fix (ComfyUI >= 0.11.1) is known.

Real regression (subgraph conversion hid multi-image inputs) directly relevant to VibeComfy's own port/convert pipeline and its flux2_klein edit templates, which take multiple images. Testing requires diffing public inputs against the older source workflow, and 'correct' input surface is only implied by the old workflow, so verifiability is medium.

Widely-hit weight/arch mismatch (Qwen3-shaped text-encoder weights into a Llama CLIPLoader) — the class of runtime loader error VibeComfy's port doctor and model checks target. Reproduction depends on ComfyUI build version and actual checkpoint files, so not repo-only testable; fix (update backend) is known but environmental.

Missing custom nodes on wan2.2 14B animate template with Manager showing nothing to install — exactly what `vibecomfy port check`/doctor/install-plan exists for, and the closest ready template (wan22_animate_native_first_stage) imports kjnodes/sam2/controlnet_aux custom nodes whose absence is trivially simulated. Verifiable right answer: install the required node packs.
Windows-embedded-python packaging issue (sqlalchemy missing for --enable-manager): ComfyUI launcher/infrastructure, no workflow or VibeComfy template surface at all.
Desktop-app GPU autodetection on mixed Nvidia+AMD hardware: installer/desktop-app infrastructure, no mapping to any workflow template or VibeComfy validation capability.

Root cause is faulty GPU VRAM (confirmed via OCCT); black/NaN outputs across SDXL/Wan/Flux2 are one user's dying 5080, not a workflow or validation problem VibeComfy can exercise. --novram workaround is hardware-scoped.

Classic stale-core version skew: KJNodes Load VAE fails on ltx_2.0_vae with outdated ComfyUI. LTX templates depend on the LTX VAE path; VibeComfy doctor/nodes install-plan can detect version-requirement gaps even though the exact RuntimeError is runtime-only. Confirmed fix (update ComfyUI core) gives a crisp right answer.

Stale-node-pack incompatibility (SimpleCalculatorKJ TypeError + VAE load fail) is fully exercisable: SimpleCalculatorKJ is used in six ready runexx templates, and VibeComfy schema validation against object_info deterministically flags missing/outdated node classes. Confirmed fix (update KJNodes/ComfyUI) is verifiable.

Wrong checkpoint/VAE pairing for a MiniMax H3 turbo-LoRA workflow is a realistic model-resolution problem, but no H3 template exists in the catalog, the error text is unknown (screenshot only), and no confirmed correct pairing was recorded.

Version-dependent LTXVAddGuideMulti error is a real node-pack skew case; the node is present in a ready template so schema/object_info validation can exercise the mismatch class. Fix (update LTXV pack) is implied but not explicitly confirmed in the record.

A template request (Kijai TTM for Wan native), not a failure: no error to reproduce, no correct answer defined, and VibeComfy ports from workflow JSON, not the attached screenshot. Only weakly maps to template-authoring capability.
Informational 'what is this DepthAnything v2 model' question, not a problem; no failure to exercise, no template uses depth models, and no verifiable solution.

21:9 aspect-ratio tensor shape mismatch in KJ ImagePad within an LTX outpainting flow; ImagePad is used in ready runexx templates so the workflow-level class (extreme-AR pad handling) is editable/testable, and the user-confirmed fix (bypass ImagePad / correct input dims) is verifiable. Triggering the exact RuntimeError needs a runtime.

Rune's prompt-enhancer meta-tensor load failure is realistic and the enhancer surface exists in six ready runexx templates; recorded likely_fix is a node/version update (unconfirmed). Exact NotImplementedError needs a GPU runtime with specific offload config, keeping reproducibility at medium.
Generic split_with_sizes error on an unspecified 'ltx workflow' — no workflow, node, or confirmed fix identified, so there is no concrete template mapping or right answer to check against.

Classic post-update VRAM/model-cache failure fixed by tiled VAE; affects z_image AND klein 9b edit (both in catalog). Failure itself is runtime/hardware-dependent so hard to trigger deterministically, but the known fix (enable tiled VAE in the template) is directly editable and validatable against image/z_image.

User-specific environment breakage (VRAM offload regressed after lora training in a separate uv env, models streaming from SSD). Real pain but it is one machine's install state, not a workflow-level problem; VibeComfy validation/port tooling cannot exercise or verify it.

MiniMaxH3 Cache custom node corrupting core ComfyUI files and breaking audio is a real class of problem (install-corrupting custom nodes). But it lives in the user's ComfyUI install, not the workflow graph; VibeComfy's graph-level validate/inspect cannot reproduce or detect it.

GGUF dequant/noise-output differing across GPUs (5070 Ti noisy, 3060 fine) maps to the only GGUF t2i template. But reproduction requires specific hardware and the 'right answer' is not established; duplicate of a single report.
Exact duplicate of scenario 3 (same message_id). Same hardware-dependent GGUF noise issue; keeping one occurrence is already marginal, so as a test scenario this adds no independent coverage.
Report of a silent error with 'no console errors, no red nodes' but the message never states what the error or workflow is. Nothing to map to any template or validation path; unverifiable.

Intermittent 'vram grow error' at the upscale stage mid-batch is a plausible memory-leak/growth problem for video+upscale pipelines. But it is seed/load-order dependent and needs a live ComfyUI with models to reproduce; no established fix to verify against.
Transient frontend glitch that vanishes on browser-tab reopen; the actual error is never shown. Not a workflow-level problem and untestable by VibeComfy graph validation or templates.
Third exact duplicate of the GGUF cross-GPU noise report (same message_id). Even treating it independently, it stays hardware-bound and unverified.

Z-Image Base injecting unrelated-image noise into preview frames on a specific ComfyUI version is a real version-regression class. Maps to image/z_image, but the trigger is ComfyUI/frontend-version specific, so a graph-level run of the template won't reliably reproduce it.

Real intermittent 'Tensor with 2 elements cannot be converted to Scalar' during LTXV AudioVideoMask video extension with bf16 at high steps; template with the masking node exists. But it's an intermittent nondeterministic runtime bug (requeue-dependent) with no clear known right answer, so hard to verify a fix.

Wiring LTX i2v from Kijai split (sharded/distributed) model files fails after connecting - a very common mistake; VibeComfy's native ltx2_3_i2v template is the canonical answer (use full/comfy weights, not Kijai splits). But 'an error after connecting' is underspecified - no error text or screenshot content, so exact failure mode can't be pinned.

Very realistic 'video editing drove me crazy, need a good workflow' request for MiniMax-era video editing. Maps to the v2v-extend template, but it's a workflow request with no concrete error or verifiable failure - nothing to assert a fix against.

Crash at 'Load Latent Upscale Model' node in LTX workflows is a known real issue (wrong/missing upscale checkpoint for the latent upscaler). LatentUpscale nodes are present in several LTX ready templates, so a validation check (correct upscale model name present in a lowvram variant) is exercisable; only the actual crash trace is off-screenshot.

Genuine pain (batch resize/outpaint a folder of images) and the upscale part touches basic_image_upscale, but it's a feature/capability request: VibeComfy has no outpaint or folder-batch template, and there is no failure to reproduce or right answer to check.

Real but flaky-environment problem: random VRAM growth failure at upscale init after several gens, explicitly not the usual CUDA OOM. Nondeterministic VRAM fragmentation on one user's box can't be reproduced deterministically by VibeComfy validation, and no stable known fix.

MiniMax H3 generations look broken/unusable on the user's VRAM-limited GGUF setup. VibeComfy has no MiniMax template or external workflow, and output quality bugs need visual comparison of the attached video - nothing exercisable by template validation.

Ghosting artifact comparison on MiniMax H3 API vs local runs. No workflow error, no settings failure - purely a quality/degradation discussion with no mechanical failure mode VibeComfy can exercise, and no MiniMax coverage anyway.

Classic real problem (Chroma output blurry/fuzzy despite official workflow and exact models). But no ready template or external workflow for Chroma exists in VibeComfy, and the cause is likely a subtle quality/config issue visible only in the image - not a validation or port error.

Pastel/phosphorescent oversaturated colors on the official LTX-2 simple 1-pass I2V/T2V workflow is a well-known, widely-reported LTX quirk (gamma/color-space handling in the simple workflow) - a strong generalizable settings question. Directly exercises ltx2_3_t2v/i2v templates, though verifying the 'correct colors' fix requires visual judgement rather than a hard assertion.
Real LTX2 quality complaint (sampler/steps tuning) and ltx2 templates exist, but 'quality' has no ground truth and the workflow was never shared; verifiable only as subjective output comparison.

Plausible LTX2 audio-i2v config (bf16, euler/25/CFG5, 1920x1024) maps to the iamccs audio i2v template, but no defect is described - it is a settings/prompt review request with no failure to reproduce or right answer to check.

Rebuilding a 3-sampler high-noise/low-noise cascade with a Seko LoRA producing garbage is the classic dual-noise split-inference mistake; the correct stage wiring (which pass gets the LoRA, sigma boundaries) is checkable against the Klein base/distilled pattern.

The low-res sample -> resize upscale -> re-sample with start/end step window idiom (cseti-style) is a recurring LTX pattern; the user's own hypothesis (step window breaks sigmas so it never denoises) gives a concrete, testable config for a two-pass graph.

Nondeterministic VRAM grow at upscale init is a very common runtime pain, but it is hardware/allocator-dependent and cannot be exercised by VibeComfy's graph validation or template params; no known fix to verify.
Phantom error with no console output and no red nodes, described only via a screenshot; the symptom is unspecified so there is nothing to map to any template or validation path.
Error appears 'out of nowhere' and disappears after reopening the browser tab - a Comfy frontend/session-state flake, not a workflow-level problem; unreachable by a Python graph driver.

Attention-node swap (Spectrum) giving 30% speedup but badly degraded output is a well-known backend-numerics class affecting all video diffusion; deterministic same-seed with/without comparison against a t2v template gives a checkable verdict.
'Why do I keep seeing this, does it do anything?' about an unspecified element shown only in an attached image - a curiosity question with no failure, no fix, and no identifiable mapping.
Stray nodes auto-connecting while navigating the canvas is a Comfy frontend mouse-gesture/UI regression, not a graph-semantic problem; VibeComfy drives workflow JSON and can never trigger it.

Open-ended community question asking how others do character swap with a 'ref2va turbo lora' 4-step turbo setup — no failure, no error, no broken workflow. Nothing to reproduce or verify against VibeComfy.

Classic 'is it the model, the prompt, or the workflow?' decoding-artifact question on T2V output. VibeComfy can render ltx2_3_t2v with different VAE/decoder/precision settings and compare; verified fix is the decoder/decode-path, though judging artifacts needs eyes on output.

Known real issue: SageAttention degrades T2V output ('cursed' frames) on a default workflow. VibeComfy's widget schema understands PathchSageAttentionKJ/attention_mode, so the toggle can be exercised; verdict depends on runtime output quality, not pure validation.

Broken/ugly audio on a MiniMax-H3 T2V workflow, reproducible from their pasted env (ComfyUI 0.31.0). Audio pipeline is real but MiniMax-H3 has no ready template — nearest is LTX audio templates, so reproduction is by analogy, and the audio bug is plugin/model-version sensitive.

Upscale/zoom-in 'reference workflow' produces blurred output from a clear 480p source — the canonical lossy-resample pitfall VibeComfy's basic_video_enhance encodes. Exercise by running enhance on a sharp clip and checking blur vs correct preprocessing; clear right answer (proper input handling/scale path).

First-frame doesn't match ref image when miswiring ref slots (character sheet in ref_image_1, wrong slot wiring) — a structural input-slot mistake on a first/last-frame template. VibeComfy validate/inspect flags slot misuse, and the correct wiring is deterministic; direct mapping to ltx2_3_runexx_first_last_frame.

Reproducible reported bug: detach the reference video, swap image+prompt, run — verifiable with metadata-carrying PNG workflow. VibeComfy can snapshot/validate/run this reference-to-video (VACE/wrapper) graph and the expected behavior is unambiguous; exactly the kind of structured A/B the harness is built for.

Off-by-one audio seam: a second of end-of-clip audio leaks to the start of i2v output. Real, workflow-level audio-sync defect; exercise by running an LTX audio i2v template and checking sample alignment. Fix verifiable in output audio, but needs runtime and MiniMax-specific graph is only approximated.

'im getting even weirder results with that lol... workflow issue?' with only an image attachment — no workflow, no error, no description of expected vs actual. Nothing to map to any template or validation.

Precise structural question about Bernini/Wan conditioning: per-slot image refs vs the Batch Images node feeding reference_images, with the actual JSON attached. VibeComfy validate/inspect can directly detect double-feed/unbatched multi-ref wiring, and there is one correct wiring; maps cleanly to VACE/wrapper multi-reference templates.

Classic multi-controlnet stacking question (depth vs pose, different weights). Can be exercised by building the two-WanVideoControlnet graph on the WAN controlnet template and letting validate check structure; right answer (chained conditioning / union node) is a known canonical pattern but partly quality-judged.
Vague one-liner ('trash results', PiD Nvidia model) with only a screenshot, no workflow JSON or error. No mapped template, no verifiable failure mode.
Opinion/discussion post ('is Wan dead?', LTX vs VACE comparison). Not a problem scenario; nothing to exercise or verify.

Vid2vid detailer outputs nearly identical, same-size video — classic denoise-too-low / missing latent-upscale wiring. User attached the actual workflow JSON, so inspect/validate can find the structural cause against the v2v templates; right answer is well defined.
'Muddy' output from runexx 3-pass is a perceptual quality complaint: reproducing requires real GPU generation plus visual judgment, and the message gives no workflow/config details to pin a cause.

Embeddings-connector-with-transformers-only question is a common LTX 2.3 config issue. inspect can compare connector presence across ready templates (which encode the canonical wiring); the runtime half of the answer still needs a GPU run.

Full-model worse than Q4 GGUF, suspecting VRAM optimization — real hardware-dependent issue; low_ram templates encode the knobs but confirming degradation needs GPU runs on constrained VRAM, and no crisp right answer is checkable.
Odd colors in second pass of official 2pass fp8 workflow — again a perceptual color-shift symptom; nothing for validate/port to catch and no clearly verifiable fix from the message.

Classic LTX two-stage complaint: stage-1 fine, stage-2 colors broken. Maps directly to the two-stage ready template; exercising requires a GPU run to observe the quality regression, so verification is semi-subjective.

Advanced user merging FML + IC-LoRA + Depth-Anything control (VACE-style multi-condition). Maps to the IC-LoRA control templates and VibeComfy's graph composition/validation; success is judged on output quality, so no crisp right answer.
